title: Chapter 24: The Morning He Yearned For
content:
Chapter 24:

The Morning He Yearned For

Having formed a contract with Beatrice, Subaru obtained a very small measure of peace.

However, regarding the essential point that he was cornered, the situation hadn’t improved one bit, nor was a solution even remotely in sight.

As usual, Subaru continued his shut-in life, unable to leave the guest room, and Beatrice wasn’t sticking to Subaru twenty-four seven either.

In fact, because he had negotiated for her to allocate her guard duties to the critical time—from the night of the fourth day to the fifth day—Beatrice, who didn’t want to be by Subaru’s side if she could help it, hadn’t come to his room even once since that incident.

Instead, the one visiting Subaru time and again was,

“I see, that’s good. Beatrice properly came to apologize. I’m impressed, impressed.”

Emilia, nodding with a smile on her face beside his bed.

Her frequent visits pricked Subaru’s conscience, and at the same time, she seemed like a goddess without exaggeration, bringing a single ray of light to this world that was nothing but darkness.

Despite being pushed away with such harshness, Emilia still walked toward Subaru. Even when he voiced a succinct apology out of guilt,

“You were surely just on edge, right? Everyone has times like that, so it can’t be helped. Though I’d be happy if you said that to Ram and Rem, too.”

She gently let Subaru’s rude remarks slide.

Regarding her modest request after that, Subaru couldn’t return a clear answer.

Purely speaking, if they judged him as an untrustworthy element who knew the circumstances, Subaru’s mouth would be silenced by them. On the other hand, it was also the honest truth that even after tasting their excessive loyalty, he couldn’t bring himself to hate the two of them completely.

Although, perhaps that was a cardboard hope born from the optimistic thought that only one of them was definitely involved, and maybe the other knew nothing.

Day by day, Subaru wore down his spirit between hope and the disappointment that outweighed it.

Emilia stared intently at Subaru as he grew gaunt, then glanced at the meal placed beside the bed, and said,

“As I thought, you haven’t eaten your food.”

“…………My bad.”

Subaru was a guest who was nothing but trouble. Despite not allowing the mansion’s servants to see his face, and on top of that, greeting their first meeting with abuse, they did not commit the injustice of cutting corners on his meals, as was proper.

Even though the meals served went almost untouched every time, and he knew he was clearly unwelcome, they fulfilled their duties without changing their expressions or voicing a single complaint.

He knew that one was blunt and the other was politely rude, but neither had a personality that would cut corners on work. Subaru knew that. And yet,

—Isn’t there poison in it?

Every time he looked at the food, such anxiety crossed his mind.

He didn’t think they were the type of opponents to use such methods. If they were going to do that, there should have been any number of chances in the loops so far.

But their actions had always visited Subaru directly. Therefore, he was half-convinced that when they came to kill him this time too, they would come gripping a weapon.

The reality that people he knew had many good points were definitely trying to kill him. Subaru’s despair began from the point of acknowledging that.

Because he was in such a mental state, the reason he couldn’t stomach food was purely that his internal organs couldn’t fully suppress their trembling due to tension and anxiety.

He thought the food was surely delicious. It was a taste he had realized was good again and again. He might have even thought that eventually, he would be able to cook just as well.

“If you don’t eat even a little, it’s poison for your body, you know? It might be hard, but…”

“My stomach won’t accept it… If Emilia-tan feeds me with an ‘aahn’, I might be able to eat.”

Throwing a worthless quip at her sorrowful face, Subaru cursed his own unsalvageable nature.

At himself, a failure who could no longer even feign his usual frivolity toward someone who was likely genuinely worried about his well-being.

However,

“Okay then, here, 

aahn

.”

“——Huh?”

“Come on, 

aahn

.”

Placing the tray with the meal on her lap, Emilia was looking at Subaru with a spoon in her hand.

Soup was scooped into the spoon, and still barely retaining warmth, it aimed for Subaru’s mouth, slowly approaching him.

Not understanding Emilia’s intention, Subaru frantically waved his hands,

“No, no no no, wait a sec, Emilia-tan. What are you doing?”

“What am I doing? Subaru, you said you’d eat if I did this, didn’t you? So, eat. I’m doing ‘aahn’ for you.”

“Uhh, regarding this sort of thing, there’s a certain aesthetic beauty in the fact that somehow or other you can’t actually do it in the end, or even if you do do it, there’s something moving about the girl turning bright red and reaching her limit after one time, you know?”

“There’s no way I’d be embarrassed just feeding a little bit of food to a boy saying such childish things. Come on, stop talking nonsense.”

Against a flustered Subaru, Emilia forcibly enforced the ‘aahn’. Eventually pushed by her vigor, Subaru felt his ears heating up with shame as,

“A-Aahn.”

“Okay, gulp. I’m keeping them coming, okay? Here, here, here, here, here.”

“Too fast!? It’s my first aahn, yet there’s no lingering sentiment or anything!?”

Mechanical and efficient movements, as if they were holding a speed-eating championship. Instinctively putting the spoons thrust out one after another into his mouth, Subaru, who had fallen into Emilia’s trap, reached the point of finishing the meal by her hand.

Splendidly emptying the tray, a satisfied-looking Emilia deepened her smile with a “Yep,” and,

“Come on, what do you say when you finish eating?”

“Thanks for the grub.”

“Bad manners. Correctly, once more.”

“Thank you for the meal.”

“Okay, you’re very welcome.”

Emilia bowed politely to Subaru, who bowed his head deeply.

As for Subaru, a strange sense of fullness was pressuring his internal organs because he had suddenly stuffed food into an empty stomach that had endured for over two days.

To Subaru, who tilted his head wondering since he didn’t recall eating a significant amount,

“Since you haven’t eaten anything proper for a while, this is so your stomach won’t be shocked. Ram suggested it, and Rem made it. Because they’re good girls.”

Emilia’s words, sounding as if she were boasting of sisters, pierced sharply into Subaru’s chest.

Consideration that should have surely made him happy enough to cry if it were true, now became nothing but a painful delusion to the current Subaru, enough to make him cry for a different reason.

Behind the kindness, behind the friendly behavior, there is a reverse side that is not as it seems.

Yes, once he had been made to realize that.

“Now then, I’ve fed Subaru, and if I stay too long I’ll probably tire you out, so I’ll head back.”

“If you like, you can sleep next to me, you know?”

“I’m glad you seem to be getting your energy back. But I have a lot of things I need to do, too. Since I’m sneaking out, I can’t really.”

Emilia closed one eye, apologizing for her playfulness.

Suddenly recalling her schedule for this time of day up until now, Subaru realized how blessed he was.

At this time, she should have been constantly chased by studies in her own room.

To shoulder a country, to aim for the future, she should have been piling up diligent efforts.

To waste even a second paying attention to a loser of fate who had nothing but his body, couldn’t advance to the future, and kept repeating the present—it must be precious time.

Suddenly, someone whispered in Subaru’s heart, asking if he was fine with keeping on losing to fate.

Raising his head as if pushed in the back by that competitive spirit, which sounded exactly like his own voice,

“Hey, Puck.”

“…I was keeping quiet because my loveliness doesn’t fit the atmosphere, so what’s uuuup?”

The silver hair holding the tray was about to leave the room. He called out to her back by another name, and watched as a small kitten appeared, parting the long silver hair.

Looking firmly into those black eyes, Subaru pointed at him and said,

“Nothing will probably happen to Emilia-tan, but… protect her properly and thoroughly. Even if you have to use that small body as a shield.”

“Saying I can protect her with my size, that’s quite a small crisis, isn’t it?”

“Shut up. Just, I’m counting on you. This time, I’m full up just dealing with myself.”

He didn’t think a crisis would reach Emilia.

At least, Roswaal had no reason to harm her, and if Roswaal didn’t, those twins wouldn’t birth a reason either.

The only one in danger of their life in this mansion was, frankly, Subaru alone.

“Worrying only about your own life, huh? That’s simple… No, wait. Thinking about it carefully, I feel like I didn’t do anything that big last time either.”

He had a premonition that the summary of the last loop was that while he was weathering the situation on momentum, a handsome guy swept everything away.

Last time and this time, wasn’t Subaru just being jerked around?

“I’m sorry to interrupt while you’re confused in a good way, but I’ll properly accept your advice. —Yeah, since it doesn’t seem to be a lie or malice.”

Softly, slightly lowering the tone of his voice, Puck nodded.

Wondering what he was thinking behind those pitch-black pupils where no light entered, Subaru pulled in his chin as that emotionless look seemed both eerie and reliable.

At the exchange between the two, Emilia, who had been left behind despite being the subject, pursed her lips in dissatisfaction,

“Reaching an understanding just between the two of you, what is it? Are you thinking of something bad?”

“No way, no way. It’s talk about how since you’re a girl, let’s be careful about various things. Watch out for cars, watch out for men!”

“Cars… do you mean carriages or dragon carriages? What does ‘watch out for men’ mean?”

“Since not all men are single-minded and sincere like me, it’s talk saying listen well to your father’s stories, and judge whether they’re someone you can trust, Emilia-tan.”

At Subaru’s words, where his usual tone had emerged, Puck nodded deeply,

“That’s right, Lia. From now on, don’t think of my opinions as annoying nagging, and listen seriously. First, black-haired men with nasty looks in their eyes are a no-go. If you bring home someone like that, I won’t let them in the house anymore, okay?”

“Brutus, you too 

agaaaain

!”

A roar at Puck, who had slashed at the back Subaru had entrusted to him as if it were natural. One person and one animal tilted their heads at the unknown name. Subaru cleared his throat as if to pull himself together, and said,

“Anyway, that’s all. Be especially careful at night. Since Emilia-tan is cuuute, I think you’re always fighting the fear of unwanted night visits, though.”

“I hear the floor my room is on is set up so that if someone trespasses, it’s conveyed to a scary guardian.”

“Close one. Good thing I’m too exhausted to do anything but sleep like a log after work. I can’t even do a night visit in peace, geez.”

“I’ll leave the lock open, so if you have the courage, you can try it, you know?”

Raising her hand slightly, Emilia left the room leaving only that behind. As she left, the kitten on her shoulder greeted him with a wave of its paw as well.

At least, he was able to call out a warning to her and her guardian.

At this rate, the two of them would probably be fine.

“Ah, crap…”

Suddenly, the moment relief pierced into his heart, drowsiness trampled over Subaru’s consciousness with a thud.

The sleep demon, which he had deflected with pain, dominated his consciousness seizing this opportunity, stripping away Subaru’s will to resist from the roots.

The fact that his hunger had been inadvertently satisfied might have also been one of the indirect causes that left him without the energy to resist it.

Thinking he couldn’t afford to sleep, as if biting his lip, Subaru’s consciousness fell sinking into a slumber.

※※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

In the rift between dreams and reality, Subaru’s consciousness drifted like a cloud.

He had heard somewhere before that the act of dreaming during sleep is a byproduct occurring as a result of the brain organizing information.

Then, the fact that scenes hindering Subaru’s peaceful sleep continued even while he slept like this made sense as the organizing of vivid memories.

The sensation of half his body being torn off, the moment his skull was smashed, the pain of his leg being blown away, the sense of loss of his throat being bored through, the despair of his stomach being slit open; they tormented Subaru, standing on the edge of dreams, even as he escaped from reality.

Groaning, having nightmares, twisting his body while soaking his whole body in sweat, spilling tears from the corners of his eyes, Subaru continued to fight the emotions welling up from within him.

It’s suffocating. It’s painful. It’s sad. It hurts. I don’t want this anymore. I want to end it.

Whining, complaints, overflowed endlessly, and each time, his soul was whittled down. Whittled down, whittled down, and in the end, it would be completely worn away and surely nothing would remain.

His mind and body were completely exhausted, enough to make him think that way.

Suddenly, the stiffness in Subaru’s body vanished.

As if the chill, the horror, that made his body tremble from the core had suddenly been swept away.

The reason was a hand.

Someone was holding Subaru’s hand.

Someone was touching Subaru’s existence, which drifted in the rift of unconsciousness within the bed, from the side of reality, trying to anchor him.

It was a warm sensation. It was a gentle sensation. It conveyed that he was being cherished.

He felt as if he had been saved. A gentle breeze blew into his desolate heart.

His pained sleeping face became peaceful, and his breathing forgot the hardships and returned to something quiet.

Who was it, he wondered. What was it, he wondered.

Was it reality, or was this also a convenient dream?

Feeling the faint warmth remaining on both his right palm and left palm—

※※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

“——How long you’re going to sleep like a log, I wonder?”

“

Bunder-sree-gah

!”

Subaru’s cry of anguish as he was violently kicked off the bed and forcibly awakened.

Roused by the hard sensation of the floor, Subaru grabbed the bed and lifted his body; before his eyes, Beatrice was standing on the opposite side across the bed.

Crossing her arms with an attitude that didn’t hide her displeasure in the slightest, she snorted haughtily and said,

“It became the promised time, so I came even though I hated it, in fact.”

“There’s such a thing as hateful words without needing to hit someone, you know. It feels exactly like that right now.”

Throwing his upper body onto the bed, Subaru told her so in a tired tone.

Suddenly, he realized that he had been sleeping and his blood ran a little cold. Even though he had brought his consciousness to wakefulness so much and hadn’t lacked vigilance.

“Falling asleep on the crucial fourth day, am I seriously a reckless moron?”

“You’re noisy with your grumbling, I suppose. Come on, we’re going, in fact.”

Ignoring Subaru lamenting with his face covered by his palms, Beatrice guided his attention with a beckoning gesture and headed for the door. At her back, Subaru panicked,

“Going… where are we going?”

“Are you telling me to spend a night in a room filled with your smell, I wonder? I refuse, in fact. The place for Betty is inside the Forbidden Library; that is non-negotiable, in fact.”

Beatrice snapped her fingers lightly and touched the door.

No abnormality could be seen, but presumably, with just that, the preparations for “Door Crossing” were complete.

It was an unexpected offer from Beatrice, but Subaru was grateful for this stroke of luck. Beatrice’s “Door Crossing” could be said to be a troublesome item for attackers as it prevented them from pinpointing the location for a surprise attack. Although for some reason it didn’t work on Subaru, he had confirmed that Rem had no effective means of “Door Breaking.”

“You, you’re surprisingly thinking about various things for me, aren’t you?”

“If we don’t hurry the tea will get cold, so return quickly, in fact.”

To Subaru’s impressed voice, Beatrice gave a curt reply. It seemed that her being considerate was a misunderstanding.

Grimacing that he had wasted his breath, Subaru suddenly looked at both his hands.

There was nothing particularly different about them, but for some reason, he was terribly curious.

Come to think of it, while he was sleeping, someone, his hand…

“Beatrice. I don’t think it’s possible, but you weren’t holding the hand of the sleeping me or anything, were you?”

“That really is an impossible story, in fact. Even if Bubby asked me to, I would politely decline, I suppose.”

“You’d go that far, huh… But with a guy like me—If we die, we die together!”

“Absolutely NOT, 

in fact

.”

Subaru gave a thumbs up, his teeth gleaming weakly.

It was his usual pose, but his condition hadn’t returned yet.

Leaving a sigh of amazement at such a Subaru, Beatrice went through the door. Hurriedly fixing his appearance here and there, Subaru also crossed the door to the Forbidden Library.

As always, Subaru thought it was a room where he couldn’t wipe away the impression of both serenity and clutter.

This room, where bookshelves packed to the brim with books stood endlessly, never changed its appearance no matter how many loops he visited it in.

Beatrice, who had entered the room first, went to the side of the stepladder that was her designated spot as usual. Opposite the door, she sat on the stepladder that was abandoning its role by being treated as a chair, and,

“You should kill time appropriately, in fact. If it’s here, no matter what happens… I don’t think anything will happen, but I will keep the contract, in fact.”

“Even if you tell me to kill time…”

Tension and the anxiety accompanying it. He had been trying to regain his composure since earlier, but still, as the critical time approached, he couldn’t remain calm.

Subaru looked around the room, comparing the many books lining the shelves, and,

“That’s right. Are there books written only in ‘I-glyphs’?”

“…There are some, in fact. Don’t tell me, you can’t read other writing, I wonder?”

“Embarrassingly, yeah. But even like this, I put in effort, you know.”

With all his might, while being watched over by the twins—

He gouged his own wounds grandly by himself, and took massive damage.

“To step foot into the Forbidden Library of the Mathers family, that is a waste of a treasure, in fact. Betty inviting someone in here happens maybe once every few years or not, I suppose.”

“Even if you say that, a book I can’t read is a bundle of paper, and even if you tell me the chance to enter the Forbidden Library is precious…”

Unfortunately for Subaru, this room was neither rare nor anything special.

Even if he told the current Beatrice that, it would only complicate things, and judging that it wasn’t something to be particularly proud of, Subaru shut his mouth.

At Subaru cutting off his words halfway, Beatrice furrowed her brows suspiciously. To her, Subaru raised a finger trying to change the subject,

“Come to think of it, are you in this room all the time?”

“That is the contract, in fact.”

“A contract again. Contract, contract from such a young age… it seems you were caught by quite the skilled sales lady. Insurance agents are more skilled the louder their voices are, right?”

“It is all a contract I desired myself, I suppose.”

It was a tone that curtly refused any further mention.

Subaru nodded quietly at Beatrice’s manner of speaking, which had erased her expression, and,

“Or so the person involved testified—”

“If you don’t be quiet soon, I’ll be on the verge of annulling the contract, in fact!”

Beatrice stood up, pulled books from the shelf, and threw them at Subaru one after another.

Given that it was Beatrice, who usually hurled magic power without hesitation, relying on such physical attacks was extremely rare.

He nimbly caught the throws of the weak girl and piled them on a nearby stand. Suddenly the attacks stopped, and Subaru, knitting his eyebrows, realized belatedly.

The seven or so books thrown at him—all of them were books written only in ‘I-glyphs’.

Raising his face, Subaru turned his eyes toward Beatrice.

As if mocking Subaru for noticing her intention late, she waved her hand flutteringly, and,

“Is that okay for yoooou? It might be a little too haaaard, in faaaact?”

“

Ri-ight

. It might be too haaaard for meeee, so I might not understaaand.”

“It’s disgusting when both of us are using baby talk, in fact!”

“Good grief. I just matched you, you know. The level.”

If Subaru was going to set up a joke, he’d go back not to a baby, but to a fetus.

Communicating by pulling the umbilical cord or kicking the placenta.

At that attitude of Subaru’s, Beatrice shrugged both shoulders for real this time, and began to open a book as if she had completely given up on conversation.

Seeing her curt attitude, Subaru also sat on a nearby chair and picked up one of the books Beatrice had thrown and chosen for him.

He couldn’t possibly say words of gratitude out of embarrassment, but her thoughtfulness was genuinely making him happy.

※※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※　※

Thus, the silence in the Forbidden Library passed slowly.

Without exchanging words with each other, only the sound of turning pages at slow intervals flowed alternately through the library.

The books Beatrice chose for him were, as expected, mostly works for children like fairy tales, similar to previous times. Since ‘I-glyphs’ only meant content similar to being only in Hiragana, it was unavoidable that it would lean toward children.

Even that precious reading time ended up with Subaru’s eyes merely repeating going back and forth over the same page.

At first, he had the composure to proceed with reading, but as time passed moment by moment, such mental leeway was stripped away little by little.

—From the closed Forbidden Library, the state of the outside could not be known.

Due to the nature of the room, the Forbidden Library, which didn’t even possess windows, was a place where “time was frozen,” as Beatrice had once said.

Not in the literal sense, but at least in the sense that it felt that way.

What time was it outside now?

At the point Subaru was invited into the Forbidden Library, sunset was already close.

Thinking simply, calculation suggested it would be fine if he spent just about half a day here until Subaru greeted the morning of the fifth day.

However, placing himself in this stagnant place, he couldn’t measure the sensation of that mere half-day by himself at all.

He felt like only a short hour or so had passed since visiting this room, or perhaps he felt like he had been here for nearly ten hours.

The suffocating feeling coming from anxiety and tension also played a part in significantly lowering Subaru’s current reality recognition ability, and he could no longer trust his own judgment.

Yet, he felt guilty asking Beatrice about it.

It wasn’t feministic like he shouldn’t disturb her reading, but he was afraid that by taking such action, a change would occur.

Spending stagnant time like this was also suffocating. But if the situation fluctuated greatly at the drop of a hat—that was also terrifying.

Unable to go forward or back, he just continued to cower before the overwhelming phenomenon called time.

His fingers trying to turn the book went numb, and the tip of his tongue complained of thirst. The pounding of his heart beat out a familiar high speed, the ringing in his ears was high-pitched, and the sound of blood circulating could be heard from his entire body.

How long was he forced to endure such tension?

If the beginning was absurd, the end also had no forewarning.

“——He’s calling.”

Suddenly, such a mutter resonated quietly within the library.

Before the eyes of Subaru, who raised his head as if struck, Beatrice was closing her book and putting it aside. She hopped down lightly from the stepladder, and,

“I am being called, I suppose.”

As if forgetting the existence of the surprised Subaru, she muttered to herself and waved her finger.

Instantly, Subaru’s whole body received a sense of wrongness like space distorting.

A sensation close to floating assaulted his body from all directions, and despite it being an instant, fatigue like having been swung around and nausea spread languidly through his whole body.

Stopping his body from sliding off the chair, Subaru glared reproachfully at the ringleader, Beatrice. And when she finally noticed that gaze,

“Ah, come to think of it, you were here, in fact. I forgot, I suppose.”

“Forgetting even though I’m right in front of your eyes, that’s low grade even for a joke.”

“It’s a matter of priorities, I suppose. —Bubby is calling, in fact.”

Announcing just that, Beatrice passed by Subaru toward the door.

Reaching his hand toward her back as she tried to go outside as if it were natural, Subaru, unable to hide his irritation, said,

“H-Hey, wait! If you go outside now…”

“I don’t mind if you stay withdrew inside, in fact. If you stay here, you’ll be safe, I suppose.”

Blood rushing to his head at the phrasing that didn’t hide her contempt, Subaru stood up as if kicking the chair and chased her back. Putting his hand on the door handle, just a few seconds of hesitation.

But,

“Ah, dammit. What the hell, something like this!”

Inspiring himself with foul language, he threw the door open violently.

Immediately after—

“Ah—”

Unintentionally, a foolish voice spilled from Subaru’s mouth.

Shielding the dazzling light piercing his eyelids with his hand, he responded to the morning sun’s welcome with agitation.

Clawing the air with his hand as if to confirm, Subaru’s body tottered forward. The front of the hallway, the window overlooking the garden—in that high sky, was the sun that had just begun to rise.

It was the morning sun of the fifth day, which he had craved so much and hadn’t reached no matter how many times he tried.

“No, way… did I, cross it? The night of the fourth day…!?”

Unable to believe the result before his eyes, he slammed his hands against the window with force enough to break it and pushed it open. A cool breeze flowed in, and as his bangs were stroked by the wind, Subaru vividly sensed the smell of morning. The cold, newborn wind blew away the air of the mansion.

His legs gave way, and he went backward weakly just like that. His back hit the wall, and losing the will to stand, he slid down and collapsed.

Dumbfounded; there was no other way to express it.

It was a current situation he couldn’t have imagined, to the point where he couldn’t even distinguish between dream or reality.

He had completely given up. He had completely despaired. He was worn out.

And yet, Subaru had crossed the night of the fourth day and arrived at the fifth day.

“Ha, haha…”

Unknowingly, a dry laugh leaked from his mouth.

Once it spilled out, he couldn’t find a way to stop it anymore.

“Hihi, hahaha. Wha-at is it. Hey, what is it. Something like this, hey, haha…”

He couldn’t think of a way to put his current feelings into proper words.

Holding his knees, Subaru continued to spew out laughter as if he had lost his sanity while crouching in the hallway.

He couldn’t put it into words. It didn’t become words. Finally Subaru—

“——Subaru?”

What cut into that empty delight of Subaru’s was a voice like a silver bell.

At the end of his gaze, which he raised sluggishly, a silver-haired girl was standing deep in the hallway.

It was Emilia. On the morning of the fifth day, he was able to find her having greeted it safely.

Together, the two of them had crossed the night of the fourth day. That fact again made inexplicable emotions well up in Subaru’s heart.

However,

“Emilia…?”

In contrast to Subaru, whose heart was expanding with delight, Emilia stared at Subaru in astonishment. And then she suddenly broke into a run, rushed to the side of the sitting Subaru, and,

“Subaru… where, were you?”

“No, I was…”

“Because… no, that’s fine. It’s fine so… come with me.”

Having his hand pulled, Subaru stood up while being surprised by her forcefulness.

Just like that, without hearing Subaru’s reply, Emilia began to run down the corridor, dragging him forcibly.

While being taken aback by her sudden action, Subaru tried to mention it, but his throat stopped upon seeing Emilia’s profile.

On her refined profile, unconcealable agitation and irritation were floating.

It was an expression reminiscent of the time of the battle at the loot house.

“Hey, what on earth—”

Happened, he could not ask.

Because faster than he could voice those words, another sound struck Subaru’s eardrums.

—That was, he thought, a scream. Or perhaps, it might have been a shriek.

High-pitched and trailing, it was filled with sadness, a cry of the soul that could not help but leave painful claw marks on the hearts of those who heard it.

The scream, as if half their body were being torn apart, continued endlessly, and conveyed its urgency painfully even to Subaru, who didn’t understand the situation.

Passing through the hallway, they headed to the upper floor. The second floor on the east side was the floor where the servants’ individual rooms were. Passing a room where Subaru had been staying until a few days ago, what Emilia aimed for while pulling his hand was further in—there,

“With Roswaal…”

Blue indigo long hair stood in the hallway, narrowing his eyes at Emilia and Subaru rushing over. Right beside him, Beatrice, who had disappeared, was leaning her back against the wall, and in her hands, he could see a cat with gray fur curling its body into a ball.

“Inside.”

To Subaru, who arrived at the three of them and tried to demand the circumstances, Roswaal responded shortly with just a single word.

What he indicated was right next to him, a single private room with its door opened.

When he turned to Emilia, she also nodded to Subaru. Those violet eyes were moist, forcing Subaru to make a decision whether he liked it or not.

Swallowing his breath, Subaru turned his feet toward the inside of the room.

Even while he was stepping in, the scream from earlier continued without interruption. And it was clear that it was now hearing from the room in front of him.

Entering inside, eyelids closed from tension—opening them softly, Subaru saw.

It was a beautifully tidy room. The occupant’s methodical personality was reflected; the private room with few furnishings arranged tastefully showed that the limited space was used functionally without waste.

Though the layout itself was almost identical to the room Subaru had been using, he thought, he thought, does this much personality come out just by having a different occupant?

By thinking that, Subaru forgot the scene before his eyes for just an instant.

But such escape from reality was in vain; the world forced a conclusion onto Subaru.

In the center of the private room, there was a carefully made bed.

On top of that bed,

“

AaaaaAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAaaaaahhh—!

”

There was Ram, screaming as if to tear her throat apart in deep, deep sadness, shedding tears like rain—and.

—While being clung to by her, Rem lay there, having breathed her last.
